quests.sentence: I called her at nine this morning.
quests.ruleExplanation: Called is the simple past form, used because the sentence names a precise past time.
quests.nativeTip: Notice the specific, named time in this sentence.
quests.example: I called her at nine this morning.

quests.sentence: I've called her three times today.
quests.ruleExplanation: Have called is the present perfect form, describing repeated actions within a period that hasn't ended.
quests.nativeTip: 'Today' is still an open, unfinished period, and no single time is named.
quests.example: I've called her three times today.

quests.sentence: I called her right after lunch, but she didn't pick up.
quests.ruleExplanation: Called is the simple past form, describing a specific completed attempt.
quests.nativeTip: This refers to one specific attempt at a known point in the day.
quests.example: I called her right after lunch, but she didn't pick up.

quests.sentence: Scientists have discovered a new species of frog in the rainforest.
quests.ruleExplanation: Have discovered is the present perfect form, used for a recent finding still relevant to the present.
quests.nativeTip: This is being treated as recent, newsworthy information relevant right now.
quests.example: Scientists have discovered a new species of frog in the rainforest.

quests.sentence: Darwin developed his theory of evolution in the nineteenth century.
quests.ruleExplanation: Developed is the simple past form, describing a completed historical event.
quests.nativeTip: This is a finished historical fact tied to a specific era, not recent news.
quests.example: Darwin developed his theory of evolution in the nineteenth century.

quests.sentence: Researchers have published groundbreaking results this week.
quests.ruleExplanation: Have published is the present perfect form, connecting a recent event to the present moment.
quests.nativeTip: 'This week' is still ongoing, and the news is fresh.
quests.example: Researchers have published groundbreaking results this week.

quests.sentence: I haven't eaten anything since breakfast.
quests.ruleExplanation: Haven't eaten is the present perfect form, describing a situation continuing from a past point to the present.
quests.nativeTip: This period of not eating continues right up to now.
quests.example: I haven't eaten anything since breakfast.

quests.sentence: I didn't eat anything between breakfast and lunch yesterday.
quests.ruleExplanation: Didn't eat is the simple past form, describing a finished period with no connection to now.
quests.nativeTip: This period is entirely in the past and already finished.
quests.example: I didn't eat anything between breakfast and lunch yesterday.

quests.sentence: This year, the company has hired over fifty new employees.
quests.ruleExplanation: Has hired is the present perfect form, fitting an unfinished time period like 'this year'.
quests.nativeTip: 'This year' hasn't ended yet.
quests.example: This year, the company has hired over fifty new employees.

quests.sentence: I've eaten sushi plenty of times.
quests.ruleExplanation: Have eaten is the present perfect form, describing repeated experience without naming a specific time.
quests.nativeTip: This is about general experience, not one specific occasion.
quests.example: I've eaten sushi plenty of times.

quests.sentence: I ate sushi for the first time at a restaurant in Osaka.
quests.ruleExplanation: Ate is the simple past form, describing a single specific past event.
quests.nativeTip: This names one specific, memorable occasion.
quests.example: I ate sushi for the first time at a restaurant in Osaka.

quests.sentence: Have you tried the new café on Fifth Street?
quests.ruleExplanation: Have tried is the present perfect form, used to ask about experience without a fixed time.
quests.nativeTip: This question is about experience up to now, with no specific time mentioned.
quests.example: Have you tried the new café on Fifth Street?

quests.sentence: I graduated from university in 2019.
quests.ruleExplanation: Graduated is the simple past form, required because a specific past year is named.
quests.nativeTip: Notice the specific year named here, even though the achievement feels significant.
quests.example: I graduated from university in 2019.

quests.sentence: I've lived abroad twice in my life.
quests.ruleExplanation: Have lived is the present perfect form, describing life experience without naming a specific time.
quests.nativeTip: No specific time is given — this is about experience across a lifetime.
quests.example: I've lived abroad twice in my life.

quests.sentence: We moved into this house five years ago.
quests.ruleExplanation: Moved is the simple past form, required because a specific past time is stated.
quests.nativeTip: 'Five years ago' is a specific point in time.
quests.example: We moved into this house five years ago.

quests.sentence: The store had already closed by the time we got there.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had closed is the past perfect form, showing the closing happened before our arrival.
quests.nativeTip: One event was complete before the other past event happened.
quests.example: The store had already closed by the time we got there.

quests.sentence: We got there around nine, right after closing time.
quests.ruleExplanation: Got is the simple past form, describing an event whose place in the sequence is already obvious.
quests.nativeTip: The order is already clear from the context, so no earlier-past form is needed.
quests.example: We got there around nine, right after closing time.

quests.sentence: I didn't recognize the address because I had never been to that part of town.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had never been is the past perfect form, explaining an earlier lack of experience behind a later past reaction.
quests.nativeTip: The lack of experience goes back before the moment of not recognizing it.
quests.example: I didn't recognize the address because I had never been to that part of town.

quests.sentence: I opened the email and immediately called the client.
quests.ruleExplanation: Opened and called are simple past forms, describing a straightforward sequence of events.
quests.nativeTip: These two actions happened one after another in a clear, natural order.
quests.example: I opened the email and immediately called the client.

quests.sentence: I had already called the client before I even opened the email — someone had tipped me off.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had called is the past perfect form, emphasizing that the call happened before the unexpected earlier point.
quests.nativeTip: This time, the usual order is reversed, so the earlier action needs marking.
quests.example: I had already called the client before I even opened the email — someone had tipped me off.

quests.sentence: By the time I opened the email, the client had already resolved the issue elsewhere.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had resolved is the past perfect form, showing the resolution happened before the email was opened.
quests.nativeTip: One event was finished before another past event took place.
quests.example: By the time I opened the email, the client had already resolved the issue elsewhere.

quests.sentence: By the time we land, the connecting flight will have already departed.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will have departed is the future perfect form, describing an action completed before a future event.
quests.nativeTip: Landing is the reference point, and the departure happens before it.
quests.example: By the time we land, the connecting flight will have already departed.

quests.sentence: Our flight will depart on time, according to the app.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will depart is the simple future form, describing one planned future action.
quests.nativeTip: This is a single planned event without another future point to compare it to.
quests.example: Our flight will depart on time, according to the app.

quests.sentence: We will probably miss the connection.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will miss is the simple future form, describing a general prediction about the future.
quests.nativeTip: This is a general prediction, not measured against a specific future reference point.
quests.example: We will probably miss the connection.

quests.sentence: The bakery has sold out of croissants every day this week.
quests.ruleExplanation: Has sold out is the present perfect form, describing a repeated pattern within an unfinished period.
quests.nativeTip: 'This week' is still ongoing, and the pattern continues.
quests.example: The bakery has sold out of croissants every day this week.

quests.sentence: The bakery sold out of croissants by 8 a.m. yesterday.
quests.ruleExplanation: Sold out is the simple past form, describing a completed event on a finished day.
quests.nativeTip: 'Yesterday' is a finished day.
quests.example: The bakery sold out of croissants by 8 a.m. yesterday.

quests.sentence: By the time it opens tomorrow, the bakery will have already prepared a double batch.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will have prepared is the future perfect form, describing a task completed before a future point.
quests.nativeTip: Opening time tomorrow is the point by which the preparation will be finished.
quests.example: By the time it opens tomorrow, the bakery will have already prepared a double batch.

quests.sentence: The client hasn't responded to our last three emails.
quests.ruleExplanation: Hasn't responded is the negative present perfect form, describing a situation continuing up to the present.
quests.nativeTip: This situation is ongoing and still true right now.
quests.example: The client hasn't responded to our last three emails.

quests.sentence: The client responded within an hour the last time we reached out, back in March.
quests.ruleExplanation: Responded is the simple past form, describing one completed event at a stated past time.
quests.nativeTip: 'Back in March' names a specific finished instance.
quests.example: The client responded within an hour the last time we reached out, back in March.

quests.sentence: By the time we follow up again, it will have been over two weeks since our last email.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will have been is the future perfect form, measuring a duration that will be complete by a future point.
quests.nativeTip: The follow-up is the future point by which this duration will be reached.
quests.example: By the time we follow up again, it will have been over two weeks since our last email.
